I have independently reviewed the **clinic appointments app** against its product specification (`PRODUCT.md`), architectural invariants (`ARCHITECTURE.md`), UX walkthrough (`ux-walkthrough.md`), and server/store codebase without making any modifications to the product code.

The release verdict has been written to [REVIEW.md](file:///C:/tmp/agent-skills-eval-789V9T/workspace/REVIEW.md).

---

### **Release Verdict Summary: `BLOCK`**

#### **What Was Verified & Discovered:**
1. **Broken Confidentiality & Authorization Boundaries:**
   - [`GET /api/appointments/:id`](file:///C:/tmp/agent-skills-eval-789V9T/workspace/src/server.js#L25-L28) fetches appointment data by ID without verifying if the record belongs to the signed-in session patient (`req.session.patientId`).
   - [`POST /api/appointments/:id/notes`](file:///C:/tmp/agent-skills-eval-789V9T/workspace/src/server.js#L30-L33) allows any authenticated patient to append notes to any other patient's record.
   - This directly violates the core success criterion defined in `PRODUCT.md` (*"A patient can see their own appointments and notes, and cannot see anyone else's"*).

2. **Missing / Incomplete Frontend:**
   - [`public/index.html`](file:///C:/tmp/agent-skills-eval-789V9T/workspace/public/index.html) is an empty template containing only `<main id="app"></main>` without client scripts or stylesheets.
   - [`src/server.js`](file:///C:/tmp/agent-skills-eval-789V9T/workspace/src/server.js) does not serve static assets from `public/`.
   - The steps in `ux-walkthrough.md` cannot be executed by end-users.

3. **Session Cookie Misconfiguration:**
   - `express-session` sets `cookie: { secure: true }` without HTTPS server configuration, breaking session persistence over default HTTP.
